findings.title: Possible NPE when the Clients type resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(client, scope), if the per-client resource is not found, the code loads the "Clients" type resource via getResourceTypeResource. That method returns null when the schema is unsupported or the resource is absent. The result is passed straight to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later to resource.getScopes(), which causes a NullPointerException and a 500 instead of a clean deny.

findings.title: Per-client resource lookup does not fall back to the all-clients permission
findings.body: If a per-client resource exists (for example one with only a CONFIGURE permission), evaluation uses only that resource. A MANAGE or VIEW permission granted on all clients is never consulted for that client. The users flow handles this fallback, so a client with its own resource can be denied despite an all-clients grant. The negative-permission semantics also differ from users.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports
findings.body: getEvaluationContext is never used. The imports Scope, TOKEN_EXCHANGE, the Logger field, ClientModelIdentity and DefaultEvaluationContext are also unused. Remove them.

findings.title: isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled throw UnsupportedOperationException
findings.body: The ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). With V2 this now throws UnsupportedOperationException, because AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2. The event listener is gated only by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check, which is true when V2 is enabled. Deleting a client or role can therefore fail. Other callers, such as the client representation's authorization-permissions-enabled handling, would hit the same exception.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns resource names, which are client internal IDs, and may miss per-client resources
findings.body: findByType is applied to the type "Clients", and the resource name is added to the result. The all-clients resource itself may match that type, so the name "Clients" can end up in the result set. A client that is covered only by an all-clients permission and has no per-client resource is not listed. This weakens list and search for clients.
